identity.title: JCMT POL-2 and ALMA Polarimetric Observations of 6000-100 au Scales in the Protostar B335: Linking Magnetic Field and Gas Kinematics in Observations and MHD Simulations

paper_type_evidence.quote: We present our analysis of the magnetic field structures from 6000 au to 100 au scales in the Class 0 protostar B335 inferred from our JCMT POL-2 observations and the ALMA archival polarimetric data.

evidence.quote: B335 is an isolated Bok globule with an embedded Class 0 protostar at a distance of 100 pc
B335 is an isolated Bok globule with an embedded Class 0 protostar at a distance of 100 pc

question.value: How do magnetic field strength and field-matter coupling in the Class 0 protostar B335, inferred from JCMT/ALMA polarimetry compared with MHD simulations, relate to the observed gas kinematics?

evidence.quote: Therefore, linking observational results of magnetic field structures and gas kinematics could shed light on the role of the magnetic field in the dynamics of collapsing cores.

claims.hypothesis: Is the 6000 au field in B335 aligned with the outflow and pinched?
claims.experiment: JCMT POL-2 850 um compared to synthetic maps
claims.result: Mean PA 92 deg (std 12) vs outflow PA 90-99; all models fit equally
claims.finding: Field on 6000 au scale is pinched and aligned with outflow; JCMT cannot discriminate field strength

evidence.quote: the magnetic field on a 6000 au scale is pinched and well aligned with the direction of the bipolar outflow within a few degrees on the plane of the sky

claims.hypothesis: What field strength do the ALMA polarization data favor?
claims.experiment: Compare PA distributions with MHD models
claims.result: Central segments parallel to midplane only in lambda=9.6 at 0.1 Msun
claims.finding: Weak field lambda = 9.6 favored by polarimetry

evidence.quote: the presence of the magnetic field orientations parallel to the midplane observed around the center can only be explained with the models with initial $\lambda$ of 9.6

claims.hypothesis: Do gas kinematics agree with the weak field?
claims.experiment: Compare simulated rotation velocities and disk sizes with observations
claims.result: Weak-field models over-rotate and form larger disks
claims.finding: Kinematics favor lambda < 4.8; tension with polarimetry, possibly from overestimated beta_rot or scattering

evidence.quote: the comparison of the rotational velocities in the simulations and the observations could favor the strong magnetic field of initial $\lambda < 4.8$ in B335
